user.title: How should Home Assistant connect to your ICT Protege?

menu_options.acs: Automation and Control service (recommended, needs the Automation licence)

acs.title: Automation and Control service
acs.description: Uses the panel's Automation and Control service. Every door, area, input and output is found automatically.

data_description.host: IP address or hostname of the Protege controller.
data_description.port: The IP Port set on the Automation and Control service (usually 21000).
data_description.pin: A user PIN with rights to doors, outputs and bypass. It does not need arm or disarm rights: arming always asks for the person's own code.

web.title: Web interface only
web.description:
For controllers without the Automation and Integration licence. If yours has it, go back and choose the Automation and Control service instead: it is pushed live, while the web interface has to be polled every couple of seconds.

Create a WX operator just for Home Assistant, with rights to view status and the event log and to control only the areas, doors and outputs you want. Don't give it programming or user management rights. A session timeout of about 15 minutes is a good choice. HTTPS must be enabled (firmware 4.00.1676 or later).

data_description.code_mode: The web interface arms as the operator and never sees a code, so Home Assistant checks it. Add people and their codes under Configure afterwards.

reauth_confirm.title: Operator login rejected
reauth_confirm.description: The web interface rejected the operator name or password. Logins have stopped so the operator doesn't get locked out. Enter the details again.

error.cannot_connect: Could not connect. Check the host, the port, and that the Automation and Control service is enabled.
error.panel_error: The panel refused a request. Check that "Allow Status Requests When Not Logged In" is enabled on the service, and the logs for details.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. See the logs for details.
error.web_invalid_auth: The web interface rejected this operator name or password.

abort.already_configured: This panel is already set up.
abort.wrong_panel: That address belongs to a different panel.

menu_options.names: Names and zone settings (WX web interface)

names.title: Names and zone settings from the WX web interface
names.description: The control service has no names or zone settings, so they are read from the controller's web interface. Create a WX operator that can only view programming, and enter it here. It logs in on every start and when you press Rescan, reads names, each input's areas and input types, then logs out. Names you change in Home Assistant are kept. Leave both fields empty to stop.

data_description.wx_port: HTTPS must be enabled on the controller. Usually 443.

events.title: Event logging
events.description: Optional. Add a second Automation and Control service on the panel with its own port, and a view-only user with no control rights. The integration stays logged in on that service only to receive system events. Leave both fields empty to turn event logging off.

codes.title: Arming codes
codes.description: In web-only mode the panel never sees a code, so Home Assistant checks it. People with codes: {people}.

data_description.add_code: At least 4 digits. Stored only as a salted hash.

error.wx_invalid_auth: The web interface rejected this operator name or password.
error.wx_cannot_connect: Could not reach the web interface over HTTPS on that port.
error.code_incomplete: Enter both a name and a code.
error.code_name_taken: That person already has a code. Remove it first to change it.
